feed.title: Running Core's real consensus code inside a zkVM

entry.title: Running Core's real consensus code inside a zkVM
entry.summary:
Exploring the potential of light clients for Rootstock has been a significant area of focus recently. The innovative approach involves evaluating the costs associated with generating proofs, which is essential for optimizing performance and feasibility in real-world applications. Additionally, the ability to utilize proof of Bitcoin chain state stands out as a pivotal development. This capability allows for an examination of merge mining information contained within the coinbase, facilitating a form of ad hoc hash rate-based checkpointing. Such a mechanism could dramatically reduce the number of blocks that need to be verified, scaling down from tens of millions to just a few thousand covering recent weeks.
Moreover, the strategic importance of proving sidechains within Zero-Knowledge Virtual Machines (ZKVMs) is underscored as BitVM bridges continue to develop and mature. This progression indicates a growing need for economically viable solutions in the verification of sidechain transactions, which will likely play a crucial role in the broader adoption and functionality of blockchain technologies across various platforms. As these technologies evolve, the integration of efficient verification processes in ZKVMs will become increasingly critical in ensuring the security and scalability of sidechains.
